name: Science fiction in four parts
hint: The new thing, its consequences, the crisis and the new world: one idea followed to its end.

parts.title: The new thing
chapters: A world in motion
(ca 3 %) The main character in the middle of a concrete task in an unfamiliar everyday life. The details hint at the world without explaining it.
The novum
(ca 10 %) The new thing appears, or its first unexpected effect, and the reader understands that something has changed.
The personal stake
(ca 15 %) The new thing touches the main character directly, and we see what they stand to lose.
The way in
(ca 25 %) They make the decision that ties them to the question, and there is no way back.

parts.title: The consequences
chapters: The rules
(ca 32 %) They learn how the new thing works through trial and error, not through a lecture.
Ripples
(ca 40 %) Consequences at the second and third remove: who wins, who loses and what breaks.
Wonder
(ca 45 %) A scene of scale and wonder, where the reader sees what the new thing makes possible.
The midpoint
(ca 50 %) A reveal about what the new thing really is, or really costs, turns the whole question around.

parts.title: The crisis
chapters: The system strikes back
(ca 60 %) Those in power, institutions or the technology itself respond, and the stakes grow.
The logical consequence
(ca 70 %) The rules are followed to their uncomfortable conclusion: the worst that can happen, by the world's own logic.
The lowest point
(ca 78 %) They lose what they were holding on to, and the old solution no longer works.
The answer in the rules
(ca 85 %) They find the solution in something the reader already understands about the new thing. No new inventions.

parts.title: The new world
chapters: The decision
(ca 92 %) The main character acts and pays for it. A human choice decides, not just the technology.
Afterwards
(ca 98 %) The world and the person after the change. Answer the book's what if, or leave a question the reader carries with them.
